title: Embed latency jitter source mapping & quantized-kernel experiment plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last month we have observed elevated embedding endpoint latency jitter (wide variance between p50/p95/p99) for small-batch inference traffic originating from the hosted API. Surface metrics show stable median but noisy tails during low QPS bursts and post-autoscaling transitions. This ticket aims to map the sources of jitter end-to-end and run controlled experiments with quantized kernels, thread pinning, and micro-batch shaping to reduce p95/p99 without increasing median latency.

Scope:
- Instrument and attribute latency across stages: network enqueue, RPC/deserialize, scheduling/coalescing, kernel execution, KV-cache lookup, and post-process serialization.
- Run kernel-level experiments: quantized kernel fast-path vs fallback, alternate GEMM kernels, and vectorized prefetch knobs.
- Evaluate micro-batching strategies: timer-based coalescing window tuning, size-based shaping, and priority small-request fast-path.
- Propose safe rollout: A/B canary with monitoring and automatic rollback on embedding-quality or latency regressions.

Non-goals: full redesign of queuing architecture or large changes to API contract in this sprint.

Why this is different: previous tickets primarily targeted embedding coalescing and general microbatch schedulers. This work focuses on jitter source mapping (correlating OS/thread/socket effects and kernel fallback events) and a short experiment battery targeted at quantized kernel behavior under low-batch scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Create end-to-end tracing spans for embedding requests that show per-stage latency and relevant tags (kernel_id, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, node_numa, thread_cpu).
Run 3 controlled experiments (quantized kernel + pinning, timer tuning, priority fast-path) with reproducible workloads and publish results to the perf dashboard.
Achieve >=20% reduction in p99 for the synthetic low-burst workload used by the team (baseline measured on runtime-1.20).
No degradation in embedding vector correctness (unit check using the canonical 500-sample prompt set) beyond tolerance; document quality checks.
Design a canary rollout plan and add automatic alerting thresholds for latency/quality regressions.
work_log: 2026-02-28: Triage meeting with infra and runtime teams. Collected traces from recent incidents and agreed on tracing tags (Aisha, Marco).
2026-03-02: Replayed production sampling in staging; reproduced p99 spikes under low QPS with microbursts. Initial hypothesis: kernel fallback + socket wake latency. (Sofia)

2026-03-05: Added lightweight per-request sampling hook to surface kernel selection events and KV cache hit/miss. Early signal: ~18% of p99 events correlated with quantized->fallback transitions. (SRE + Runtime)

2026-03-09: First experiment: thread pinning + CPU isolation on staging nodes. Result: p99 down ~15% for synthetic workload; introduced small increase in median for high-concurrency tests. (bench-PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/984)

2026-03-11: Second experiment: reduce coalescer timer from 1.5ms -> 0.8ms for low-priority queue and enable priority fast-path for single-request embeddings. Observed p95 improvement but p99 still dominated by kernel fallback events. (Sofia)
2026-03-12: Started instrumenting node-level NUMA tags and socket wake metrics; found correlation between long socket wakeups and p99 in multi-socket instances. Logged a follow-up to prod infra.
next_steps: Finish kernel instrumentation to record internal fallback reasons (precision mismatch, memory format, quantization overflow).
Run quantized-kernel tuning matrix: 3 quant levels x 2 prefetch settings x 2 thread-affinity configs (total 12 runs) and publish to perf dashboard.
Coordinate with infra to test single-socket instance type for embedding small-batch workloads during canary window.
Draft canary rollout doc with monitoring runbooks and automatic rollback triggers (latency > baseline + 30% OR vector-similarity regression > 0.5% on canonical set).
